messages.text: Good speaking today. Could you put together a short proposal covering scope and pricing so I can take it to my head of ops?
Will do - I'll have a draft proposal with you by friday.
Hold off on that actually. Our budget cycle just got pushed, so we're parking all new vendor work until the next quarter. I'll come back to you in July.
Understood - I'll leave it with you. Happy to pick it up whenever.

loops.statement: send Aditya a draft proposal covering scope and pricing
loops.notes: Previously labelled superseded. Under the first-person future-tense test, "I'll have a draft proposal with you by friday" is a commitment and Aditya's "Hold off on that actually" defers it rather than cancelling it: he commits to returning in July and the user answers "Happy to pick it up whenever". The obligation survives, so the loop is open; the friday deadline does not, so certainty drops to implied with no span. July is a month-long range with no agreed endpoint, so resolved stays null.
